headline_drivers: Fiscal Q2 2026 earnings miss and gross-margin compression on May 13, 2026 (EPS €0.59 vs. ~€0.70 consensus; gross margin down 380 bps to 53.9%) triggered a sharp selloff to all‑time lows and set up the stock as a 'cheap growth' name with a forward P/E of ~14.3 (Zacks, May 21, 2026).

Despite the miss, management reaffirmed full‑year FY26 guidance for 13–15% revenue growth and 57–57.5% gross margin and highlighted 14% constant‑currency revenue growth with double‑digit growth across all regions and channels (company/ACCESSWIRE recap, May 13, 2026).

Subsequent bearish estimate cuts pushed expectations down (nine cuts to FY26 and FY27 EPS) while the fundamental guide stayed intact, creating a low‑expectations setup that attracted value and contrarian buyers once the stock based out near its lows (Zacks 'Bear of the Day', May 21, 2026).

Technical factors amplified the rebound: the stock appeared on 5‑day momentum and gap‑up/volume‑spike screens after a ~33% 5‑day rally, with RSI in the 96th percentile and volume modestly above average, consistent with short covering and mean‑reversion buying off oversold levels rather than new fundamental news.
summary: The recent 5‑day ~33% surge in BIRK is mainly a rebound from an earnings‑driven washout, not a fresh positive fundamental surprise. On May 13 the company missed Q2 EPS and showed meaningful gross‑margin pressure from FX and tariffs, but still delivered ~14% constant‑currency revenue growth and reaffirmed its 13–15% FY26 growth and margin targets. That miss drove the stock to all‑time lows and a low‑teens forward P/E, while analysts cut estimates and sentiment turned very bearish. Once the dust settled, the combination of intact growth guidance, cheap valuation, and prior oversold conditions appears to have sparked a sharp bounce, likely aided by short covering and technical/momentum buying rather than any new customer, product, or regulatory catalyst.
